leads.summary: The DKMS package drops two psmouse fixes carried by linux-omarchy
leads.consequence: On matching machines booting linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3, the packaged psmouse module from pristine upstream 7.2.3 is selected from /updates in place of linux-omarchy's psmouse. Its full source still makes an unchecked protocol_handler call during psmouse_handle_byte and uses unsigned FocalTech touch coordinates, whereas linux-omarchy's 0560-input.patch adds the disconnect guard and signed-coordinate clamp. Thus installing a touchpad enhancement reverts unrelated distribution input fixes for the entire psmouse stack on that machine. The upstream README admits this gap and expects a refresh at 7.3; decide whether to carry these two distro hunks or refresh sources before making this an automatic install. This is a source-level regression, not a claim of a reproduced crash on the T14.
leads.triage: corroborated; Opus F2; coordinator verified patch hunk, package source, dkms.conf and mainline commit message; published

leads.summary: Merging before package #472 is published prevents offline ISO builds and halts matching installs/migrations
leads.consequence: While companion omarchy-pkgs#472 remains open and unavailable in the channel's sync repository, the ISO builder adds the new package as an explicit offline download target; its pacman -Syw fails the build. A locally built runtime ISO with --local-source does not automatically build this new package: its local recipe builder only builds omarchy-settings, omarchy runtime and omarchy-nvim, so a local checkout of #472 alone is insufficient. If the runtime nevertheless reaches a matching existing installation, pacman -S of the unavailable target fails, preventing later migrations and omarchy update completion; an ISO hardware finalizer also exits nonzero. This prerequisite is already acknowledged in the PR description; ensure #472 is merged AND available on the intended mirror before this change ships, or supply a conditional/deferred path for an optional driver.
leads.triage: corroborated; Opus F1; coordinator verified build-iso.sh lines 3,190-239 and omarchy-pkgs README 25-32; published

leads.summary: Direct migrations cannot replace the previous i2c-piix4-asf-dkms package
leads.consequence: On a matching machine that still has the previous i2c-piix4-asf-dkms installed, invoking omarchy-migrate directly (including its login-time notification action) calls omarchy-pkg-add -> pacman -S --noconfirm --needed thinkpad-t14-amd-touchpad-dkms. The new package explicitly conflicts with the old one, and pacman answers No to 'Remove old?' under --noconfirm despite its replaces field: transaction aborts with unresolvable package conflicts. Bash -e prevents reboot-required and the completion marker, stops all later migrations, and the next direct run fails again. In contrast, a normal omarchy update invokes pacman -Syu first, which DOES process replaces and should replace the old package before this migration. If supporting existing users of the old package on the direct migration path matters, use the established --ask=4 swap pattern or explicitly handle that conflict, with a test for the old-package-installed state.
leads.triage: dropped; predecessor package existed only on the author's machine per #472 body; normal update path handles replaces

leads.summary: The new detector test shadows the real DMI matcher and cannot cover its product-family fallback
leads.consequence: The entire detector matrix uses a PATH stub of omarchy-hw-match that reads only TEST_PRODUCT_NAME, is case-sensitive and never reads product_family. A plausible regression that removes product_family fallback from the real helper would leave every new assertion green while skipping intended laptops whose product_name is an SKU and whose product_family contains 'ThinkPad T14 Gen 2a'. Add at least one case that exercises the production helper against distinct DMI name and family inputs (with the real helper made fixtureable), plus a case-insensitive name/family check. This is a fixture-fidelity issue, not evidence that the current helper fails; current helper checks both fields.
leads.triage: dropped; speculative mock hardening; real matcher covered by Opus dmi run; matches xps13 test precedent

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the Omarchy side (detector, hardware leaf, `all.sh` entry, ISO list entry, migration and test) follows the existing Dell XPS 13 sidecar-amps pattern and was checked in isolated command-only runs. Two points concern how this PR couples to the companion package omacom/omarchy-pkgs#472: the order in which the two ship, and a psmouse fix the package drops on `linux-omarchy`.

### A missing package affects more than the target machines

The description notes that #472 has to be merged first. The effect if the package is not yet *published* in the channel repository reaches further than the T14/P14s:

```text
omarchy-other.packages lists thinkpad-t14-amd-touchpad-dkms
  └─ ISO builder (omarchy-iso builder/build-iso.sh, set -e)
       pacman -Syw <all list entries>   -> "target not found"
       retry once                       -> fails again, unguarded
       => ISO build aborts (all hardware, not only ThinkPads)

matching existing install, omarchy-migrate
  └─ migrations/1789531418.sh -> fix-t14-...-touchpad.sh -> omarchy-pkg-add fails
       => migration stays pending, no reboot-required,
          every later migration waits behind it

matching fresh install
  └─ run_logged fix-t14-...-touchpad.sh under set -euo pipefail
       => leaf exits 1, hardware setup stops
```

The migration and leaf paths were reproduced in an isolated sandbox with a `pacman` stand-in that reports "target not found"; the ISO path is from source. Per the omarchy-pkgs README, the edge channel follows `quattro` automatically every two hours, so the gap between this PR landing and the package being published would reach edge without a manual step.

**Impact:** while a channel ships an Omarchy runtime containing this PR but its repository lacks the package, ISO builds for that channel fail and T14/P14s Gen 2a machines on it hold all later migrations. Edge is first in line, since it follows `quattro`.

**Suggested change:** sequence this PR after `thinkpad-t14-amd-touchpad-dkms` is built and published to the edge repository, not only after #472 is merged, and state the wider effect in the description so the two can be ordered deliberately.

### On `linux-omarchy`, the package drops a psmouse use-after-free fix

`linux-omarchy` 7.2.5 carries `0560-input.patch`, which backports mainline 761c2040a7d4 "Input: psmouse - fix use-after-free during protocol disconnect". The DKMS package rebuilds `psmouse` from pristine v7.2.3 sources and installs it under `/updates`, so it replaces the patched module. Excerpt, with `-` from the package's v7.2.3 source and `+` from `linux-omarchy`'s patch (the matching `psmouse_disconnect()` half is not shown):

```diff
 static int psmouse_handle_byte(struct psmouse *psmouse)
 {
-	psmouse_ret_t rc = psmouse->protocol_handler(psmouse);
+	psmouse_ret_t rc;
+	/* protocol_handler is NULL when device is being disconnected */
+	if (unlikely(!psmouse->protocol_handler)) {
+		psmouse->pktcnt = 0;
+		return 0;
+	}
+	rc = psmouse->protocol_handler(psmouse);
```

The upstream README documents this "Known gap". #472's description adds that the dropped hunks do not touch the Synaptics path, but the mainline commit message names `synaptics_disconnect()` as an example of the racing vendor disconnect handlers.

**Impact:** on T14/P14s Gen 2a machines booting `linux-omarchy`, the automatic install removes this fix until the package refreshes to a 7.3 series. This is a source-level comparison; no crash was reproduced.

**Suggested change:** carry 761c2040a7d4 as an extra patch in the package until the 7.3 refresh (the commit is in v7.3-rc1). Otherwise, correct the #472 description so the trade-off is stated accurately.

**Optional:** the migration sets `reboot-required` even when the package is already installed (for example for a second user on the same machine), which was observed in the sandbox run. Setting it only when `omarchy-pkg-missing thinkpad-t14-amd-touchpad-dkms` was true before the install would avoid the extra prompt. `migrations/1787666837.sh` behaves the same way today.

**Documentation note:** the leaf comment says the four patches are "on their way upstream", while the upstream README lists all four as "Not yet posted". Also, by #472's own measurements single-finger reports are 12.5 ms on PS/2 and 14.9 ms on SMBus, so the measured gain is in two-finger reporting (about 25 ms to 14.9 ms) rather than in the single-finger 80 Hz rate the comment cites.

**Verified:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Detector with `omarchy-hw-match`'s own matching logic (DMI path redirected), synthetic DMI/sysfs trees | matches T14 Gen 2a, P14s Gen 2a, lowercase family; rejects T14 Gen 2i, T14s Gen 2a, T14 Gen 1 AMD, L14 Gen 1 AMD, no serio devices, no `product_family` |
| Failure handling | a failing install fails the leaf; the migration sets `reboot-required` only after success and stays pending on failure |
| New test on head, and on head merged with `quattro` 387fcf59 | 14 of 14 pass |
| New test copied onto the base and onto the `quattro` tip | fails (exit 1) |
| Deliberate breakages of the detector, leaf, migration and registrations | 11 of 11 caught |
| Full `test/shell`, head vs base and merged vs tip | same failing files and `not ok` lines on each pair; the PR adds none |
